series.label: Generator fixed fee, 5 A, metered subscribers (ministry guideline)
series.notes: Fixed monthly part of the Ministry of Energy and Water's guideline tariff for METERED generator subscribers (tariff = fixed fee + metered kWh x price per kWh). 98 months, 2018-06 to 2026-07, no gaps. Basis per month in `basis`: ministry_pdf 72 (monthly tariff statement PDFs on energyandwater.gov.lb/mediafiles/prices/2-YYYY-MM-DD.pdf, the pages the HTML table leaves blank for Jan 2019 to Jul 2024), ministry_table 11 (flat figure printed in the ministry listing, Aug 2024 onward), press_relay 9 (press copies of the ministry statement: Aug and Sep 2023, Feb, Mar, Jun, Jul and Sep 2024, Sep 2025, Jul 2026), inferred_bracketed 6 (2024-04, 2024-05, 2024-10 to 2025-01: no statement read, but the fee is identical in the months on both sides; low confidence). Month is the tariff month named in the statement (statements issued on days 1-5 belong to the previous month). Several statements per month exist in late 2021 and spring 2022; the last one is kept. The 5,000 to 300,000 LBP surcharge per extra 5 A is not in this series. This is NOT the unmetered flat fee printed as `gen_5a_fixed_2013_2018_as_published` in D2 (a different, older column).

Weights change from decision to decision (see `weights_g`), so this is a price per regulated bundle, not per kg. 'Standard' means the Arabic-bread bundle of about 800-960 g: the ministry's 'large' bundle until Oct 2021, 'medium' from Nov 2021 (it gave up three classes in mid-2024 and prices one 'medium' bundle). Sources per decision in `source_by_date`. `basis`: ministry_pdf = I read the decision PDF on economy.gov.lb through web.archive.org (scans, read by eye or OCR); press = press copy of the ministry text. UNRESOLVED decisions (the ministry's own announcement titles exist in its archive but I did not retrieve the prices): Jan 2022 (a cut), 9 Jun 2022 (a cut), 7-8 Jul 2022, 19 Sep 2022 (decision 53), Apr-Nov 2023 (36,000 on 11 Apr 2023 and 45,000 in Nov 2023 are the bracketing values; the 2 Aug 2023 announcement page is not read), 4 Mar and 19 Apr 2024, 24 May 2024, mid-2021 (L'Orient Today counts 15 rises in 2021). series.label: EDL average supply hours per day, monthly proxy (energy-equivalent)
series.notes: PROXY, NOT AN OFFICIAL SERIES. Average hours per day of national EDL supply, as the energy-equivalent of full-demand supply: hours = 24 x L x G / D, with G = EDL gross energy to the grid in the month (GWh), L = 0.82 (technical losses 18 to 18.9 percent, GHG inventory Table 9), D = electricity demand in the month. D is the annual demand (24,247 GWh in 2018-19, EDF least-cost plan; 24,273 / 21,846 / 16,380 GWh in 2020 / 21 / 22, GHG inventory Table 9 citing EDL and LCEC; held at 16,380 from mid-2022; linear between mid-years) times the 2010-18 CAS seasonal shape. It is energy-equivalent, so it runs below counts of 'hours with any current' while the grid is partial (about 12 h against about 15-17 h official in 2018-19), and converges with them in the deep crisis (3.1 h in 2022 against 3.3 h reported by VASyR). G by month: CAS/EDL network supply (production plus purchases) for 2018-01 to 2019-10; BDL 'electricity production' (EDL) 2023-09 to 2025-08; CEIC public text for 2022-10 (31 GWh, the series low), 2025-11 (395) and 2025-12 (345). Months labelled in `basis`: computed = G observed that month (2018-01..2019-10, 2022-10, 2023-09..2025-08, 2025-11, 2025-12); extrapolated = 2019-11 and 2019-12 (2018 shape scaled by the 2019 Jan-Oct to 2018 Jan-Oct ratio); constrained = 2020-01..2022-09 and 2022-11..2023-08, NOT observed: smooth monthly path of hours that preserves the annual EDL totals (thermal plus hydro 12,331 / 7,654 / 2,771 GWh in 2020 / 21 / 22, GHG inventory), the 31 GWh of Oct 2022 as a floor, and the ministry or IMF statements of 3.5 h (2021-07), 4.0 h (2022-03) and 3.5 h (2023-06) as soft anchors, so the month-to-month shape inside those years is an interpolation; interpolated = 2025-09, 2025-10 (straight line in hours between 2025-08 and 2025-11) and 2026-01, 2026-03..2026-06 (line between 2025-12, 2026-02 and 2026-07); statement = 2026-02 (energy minister: 7-9 h by end February, taken as 8; a claim, and the monthly mean was probably lower) and 2026-07 (EDL on 13 Jul: about 4 h). 2026-08 and 2026-09 have no usable figure: August was a bad month (fuel delays, Tripoli at about 2 h) and September better, both without a number, so they are left out. Sensitivity: every month scales one-for-one with L and inversely with D (demand +10 percent gives hours -9 percent; losses 10 percent as in the World Bank WDI gives hours +10 percent). CROSS-CHECKS. (1) Night lights (D3-nightlights, Lebanon mean radiance, VIIRS): Pearson r = 0.92 on levels over the 86 months with both series (2018-01 to 2025-06), 0.79 on year-on-year changes (72 months), 0.94 on the 44 computed months only, 0.997 on the 8 annual means. Lights fall less than the proxy (4.50 in 2019 to 1.65 in 2022, -63 percent; proxy 12.1 to 3.1 h, -74 percent) because generators and solar also light the sky; both turn in 2022-23 and recover to mid-2025. The lights were not used to build any month. (2) Surveys: VASyR grid hours for refugee households 13 / 11 / 7 / 3.27 h (2019-22, self-reported) against proxy yearly means 12.1 / 10.2 / 7.0 / 3.1 h; HRW household survey 2.4 h in Dec 2021 (proxy 4.7 h; household average, below the national figure); ministry cut hours give about 15-17 h outside Beirut in 2018 (hours with any current, see `edl_supply_hours_ministry_outside_beirut`). (3) Statements not used as anchors: EDL said 5-6 h on 600 MW in Aug 2024 and the nationwide blackout of 17 Aug 2024 cut that month to 160 GWh (proxy 2.1 h); about 5 h in Dec 2024 (proxy 5.5 h). Where the proxy and a statement disagree by more than 2 h, trust the statement for 'hours with any current' and the proxy for energy delivered.
series.confidence: medium for computed months, low for constrained, interpolated and statement months

series.label: EDL supply hours proxy, only months with observed monthly energy
series.notes: Subset of the proxy where G was observed for the month itself (CAS 2018-01..2019-10, BDL 2023-09..2025-08, CEIC 2022-10, 2025-11, 2025-12). Method in `edl_supply_hours_proxy_monthly`.

series.label: EDL average supply hours per day, yearly mean of the monthly proxy
series.notes: Mean of the monthly proxy by calendar year; 2026 is Jan-Jul only (7 months), 2022 has the Oct-Dec collapse. Compare with the survey figures in D3 (VASyR grid hours for refugee households 13 / 11 / 7 / 3.27 h in 2019-22; HRW household survey 2.4 h in Dec 2021).

series.label: EDL gross energy to the grid used in the proxy (observed, constrained or interpolated)
series.notes: Energy behind the proxy: observed for `computed` months, back-solved from the constrained or interpolated hours otherwise (same `basis` labels as the proxy). CAS network supply 2018-19 includes purchases; BDL 2023-25 may exclude them (small after 2021).

series.label: Electricity demand used in the proxy (modelled)
series.notes: Annual demand (EDF plan 2019; GHG inventory 2020-22; held at the 2022 level afterwards) spread over months with the 2010-18 CAS seasonal shape. Modelled, not metered. Demand after 2022 is an assumption (no source), the main uncertainty of the 2023-26 proxy.
